headline_marked: [[RayNeo launches iO Smart Glasses]] for everyday use and GT series for cinema-grade AR
headline: RayNeo launches iO Smart Glasses for everyday use and GT series for cinema-grade AR
summary: The new iO Smart Glasses offer subtle AI features and real-time translation, while the GT series provides large virtual screens up to 307 inches for immersive viewing.
details: RayNeo has unveiled two distinct lines of AR smart glasses: the minimalist iO Smart Glasses and the more robust GT series. These new devices target different user needs, from subtle daily assistance to immersive media consumption.

The 33-gram iO Smart Glasses are designed for all-day wear, featuring a monochrome green display for simplified interfaces and text. They include intelligent voice capture, a quad-microphone array, and a bone conduction sensor for clear transcription in noisy environments.

The iO Smart Glasses leverage RayNeo's Ambient AI Productivity Suite to extract action items from conversations and suggest calendar updates. They also support real-time translation of 55 languages and 109 accents with minimal latency, powered by Timekettle BabelOS 3.0 AI software.

In contrast, the heavier GT series (68g for GT, 78g for GT Max) are built for focused media viewing and gaming. The RayNeo GT can project a 231-inch virtual screen with a 46-degree field of view, while the GT Max offers a 307-inch screen with a 59-degree FOV.

Both GT models feature a quad-speaker setup co-tuned by Bang and Olufsen and a 3DoF AR chip for anchoring screens in 3D space. They can also display Dolby Vision HDR content when paired with the separate RayNeo Pocket TV Pro streaming device.

RayNeo has not yet announced pricing for any of the new glasses. However, more information is expected ahead of their retail launch on September 4th, with demonstrations also planned for IFA in early September.

headline_marked: [[On-device piano autocomplete]] works with a 125M parameter model, no cloud needed
headline: On-device piano autocomplete works with a 125M parameter model, no cloud needed
summary: A developer trained a 125M parameter language model to autocomplete piano melodies, running entirely on-device without internet. This compact AI delivers real-time musical assistance without cloud dependency.
details: A developer shared on Hacker News a project where they trained a 125M parameter language model to autocomplete piano melodies. Crucially, this model runs entirely on-device, requiring no internet connection or API calls.

This project demonstrates that compact, efficient AI models can provide genuinely useful musical assistance without relying on remote servers or subscriptions. The model's size is comparable to GPT-2 Small, yet it effectively captures meaningful musical patterns.

Using a transformer-based architecture, the model treats music generation as a sequence prediction problem by tokenizing MIDI data. This approach is well-established, drawing inspiration from projects like OpenAI's MuseNet and Google Magenta.

The model was trained on a curated dataset of MIDI piano recordings, emphasizing that data quality is often more critical than model size. On-device inference offers significant advantages, including near-zero latency, making the autocomplete feel responsive.

Achieving smooth on-device performance involved serious optimization, including quantization, which reduced the model's memory footprint from roughly 500MB to about 125MB. Cross-platform inference frameworks and autoregressive streaming also contribute to its efficiency.

This tool functions as a creative assistant for musicians, suggesting musical ideas rather than replacing human creativity. It's designed to aid composition, similar to how autocomplete assists with writing emails.
